subject: DPA: EduConsortium procurement — UK data transfer & SCCs
messages:
From: Suraj Gill <suraj.gill@educonsortium.org>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, procurement@educonsortium.org
Cc: Marta Novak <marta.novak@edupartners-legal.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA & data transfer requirements for EduConsortium procurement

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement is moving quickly and we need to lock the legal terms before our board meeting on Dec 8. A few items that are blocking the purchase order:

- Data transfers: EduConsortium requires SCCs for transfers out of the UK/EU and prefers UK/EU-only hosting for student data. We need clarity on whether Redwood can commit to UK residency or if a DPA with SCCs and technical controls will suffice.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report, CAIQ/consensus answers, and a DPIA outline focusing on profiling student records.
- Subprocessors: full list and committed notification window for onboarding new subprocessors.
- Signature routing: our legal team prefers PO + DPA signature by authorized exec.

Can you confirm what you can provide by end of week? We can share a redline from our counsel if helpful.

Thanks,
Suraj
Director, Procurement — EduConsortium
[attachment: EduConsortium_DPA_request.pdf (pdf)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA & data transfer requirements for EduConsortium procurement

Suraj —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up front:
- We can offer EU/UK-only hosting on Dedicated or Private deployment for an initial pilot; hosted (public) tenancy will rely on SCCs + technical controls.
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II (attached), CAIQ responses, and a DPIA draft focused on student profiling — see linked drive.
- Subprocessor list attached; standard 30-day notice but we'll treat this as a negotiated term for enterprise deals.

I've attached a proposed DPA redline that reflects EU-only hosting options and tightened retention clauses to match education requirements. Looping in Neha (legal) and Ben (sales) to coordinate redlines and signature path.

Next steps I propose: 1) review our redline, 2) schedule a 30-min legal-to-legal call this week, and 3) confirm whether Dedicated capacity trial is acceptable for residency.

Attachments: redline_laurel_v1.docx; SOC2-TypeII-Redwood-2027.pdf

— Lauren Bishop
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Nov 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA & data transfer requirements for EduConsortium procurement

Thanks for the ping — I reviewed Lauren's redline. Quick legal notes:

- SCCs: we should attach the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (controller-processor modules) and include a UK Addendum. We can accept the customer's modular edits with two exceptions: (1) retention carveouts that exceed 180 days for logs must be justified; (2) any perpetual retention language is a hard no.
- Subprocessors: propose a 21-day notification window for high-risk subprocessors and a 30-day for routine ones; Cypress clause to allow emergency onboarding with notification after the fact.
- DPIA: we'll provide a DPIA template; if customer requires Redwood to own the DPIA we should limit scope to processor controls and how we support their assessment.
- Exception: if EduConsortium requires US outbound transfers for any student data, we need exec approval for a cross-border exception.

I've attached legal comments as PDF. If they need UK sovereign hosting, we should route to Dedicated / Private deployment procurement and provide an MSA amendment for hosting location.

Neha
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[attachment: DPA_legal_comments_2027.pdf (pdf)]

Suraj — quick commercial note from my side:

We can provision Dedicated capacity in UK region for the pilot (30 days) at a trial rate to validate latency and residency. If that works, we can convert to a reserved capacity commit tied to the MSA.

Procurement steps we typically follow: PO -> DPA + MSA sign -> provision Dedicated environment -> SOC2 evidence handoff -> production go-live. I’ve added the HubSpot deal link for your team: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/123456789/EDU-2027-3429

For signature routing, we use DocuSign for the DPA/Amendment. Our standard approach is Redwood exec sign after customer provides an authorized PO; if you need an alternate flow (e.g., simultaneous sign), flag it now and Neha can confirm.

Cheers,
Ben
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marta Novak <marta.novak@edupartners-legal.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Nov 2027 14:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA & data transfer requirements for EduConsortium procurement

Thanks all — attached is a marked-up DPA from EduConsortium counsel. Key comments from our side:

- Retention: propose turning Redwood's 180-day logs window into a 365-day audit log retention for incident investigations specific to the education environment. Please provide the technical controls that back up secure log retention and deletion processes.
- Deletion/return: require a 30-day certified deletion after contract termination for student data.
- SCCs/UK Addendum: we accept attachment but request an explicit UK Supplement that names the UK Addendum and incorporates it by reference.
- Evidence: we need SOC2 attestation plus completed CAIQ (we’ve attached a CAIQ template) and a copy of your DPIA draft before we proceed to signature.

Attached: Redline_EduConsortium_v3.docx; CAIQ_template.xlsx

Marta Novak
Counsel, EduPartners (on behalf of EduConsortium)
[attachment: Redline_EduConsortium_v3.docx (docx)]
